'''''BioShock: The Collection''''' is a 2016 [[video game compilation]] developed by Blind Squirrel Games and published by [[2K (company)|2K]]. ''The Collection'' features upgraded versions of ''[[BioShock]]'' (2007), ''[[BioShock 2]]'' (2010) and ''[[BioShock Infinite]]'' (2013), with new textures and support for higher resolution displays and framerates. The compilation was released in September 2016 for [[PlayStation 4]], [[Xbox One]], and [[Windows]]; versions for [[macOS]] and [[Nintendo Switch]] followed in August 2017 and May 2020, respectively.

A remaster of the ''[[BioShock (series)|BioShock]]'' series was widely rumored for years before its official announcement. After its release, the game was updated to address bugs and crashes. Critical reception of ''The Collection'' was generally positive, with praise focusing on the value of the collection and its appeal for new players of the franchise. Complaints included the relative lack of updates to later games in the collection, and technical performance. The game was a bestselling title in the United States and United Kingdom in its initial months of release.

== Contents ==
''BioShock: The Collection'' contains all three titles in the [[BioShock (series)|''BioShock'' series]]: ''[[BioShock]]'', ''[[BioShock 2]]'', and ''[[BioShock Infinite]]''.<ref name="Polygon: officially announced"/> The games are [[first-person shooter]]s, with a focus on story and character customization.<ref>{{cite web|last=Gerstmann|first=Jeff|date=August 22, 2007|url=https://www.gamespot.com/reviews/bioshock-review/1900-6177215/|title=BioShock Review|website=[[GameSpot]]|publisher=Red Ventures|access-date=December 23, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Sterling|first=Jim|date=February 8, 2010|url=https://www.destructoid.com/stories/review-bioshock-2-162864.phtml|title=Review: BioShock 2|website=[[Destructoid]]|publisher=Enthusiast Gaming|access-date=December 23, 2020|archive-date=September 18, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200918182814/https://www.destructoid.com/stories/review-bioshock-2-162864.phtml|url-status=dead}}</ref> Players wield guns and superpower-granting genetic modifications called Plasmids or Vigors.<ref name="arstechnica-plasmids">{{cite web|author=Westgarth, Michael|date=February 12, 2014|url=https://arstechnica.com/science/2014/02/science-is-slowly-building-towards-real-life-bioshock-like-plasmids/|title=Science inches closer to real BioShock-style plasmids|website=[[Ars Technica]]|publisher=Condé Nast|access-date=January 4, 2020|archive-date=January 9, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200109223935/https://arstechnica.com/science/2014/02/science-is-slowly-building-towards-real-life-bioshock-like-plasmids/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="gamesradar-plasmidguide">{{cite web|author=Barratt, Charlie|date=August 17, 2007|url=https://www.gamesradar.com/bioshock-plasmid-guide/|title=BioShock Plasmid Guide|website=[[GamesRadar+]]|publisher=Future Publishing|access-date=January 3, 2020|archive-date=January 3, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200103200535/https://www.gamesradar.com/bioshock-plasmid-guide/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2012-10-25 |title=Vigors - BioShock Infinite Guide |url=https://www.ign.com/wikis/bioshock-infinite/Vigors |access-date=2025-01-09 |website=IGN |language=en}}</ref> Also included in the collection are the games' single-player content originally released as exclusives or [[downloadable content]] packs, including ''[[BioShock 2: Minerva's Den]]'' and ''[[BioShock Infinite: Burial at Sea]]''. The multiplayer component of ''BioShock 2'' is not included.<ref name="Polygon: officially announced">{{cite web |last=Alexander |first=Julia |date=June 30, 2016 |url=http://www.polygon.com/2016/6/30/12064994/bioshock-the-collection-release-date |title=BioShock: The Collection officially announced |website=[[Polygon (website)|Polygon]]|publisher=Vox Media |access-date=June 30, 2016}}</ref> It includes the challenge game modes from all three releases, and the Museum of Orphaned Concepts, a feature from [[BioShock (series)#Collections|an earlier collection]] in which the player explores an in-game gallery of abandoned development concepts.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Conditt |first=Jessica |title='BioShock: The Collection' hits PS4, Xbox One and PC in September |url=https://www.engadget.com/2016-06-30-bioshock-collection-remastered-ps4-xbox-one-pc.html |access-date=December 10, 2020 |website=[[Engadget]]|date=June 30, 2016 |publisher=Verizon Media}}</ref>

''BioShock'' and ''BioShock 2'' were [[Remaster#Video games|remastered]] for the collection, with higher-resolution textures and new effects. The collection adds a [[audio commentary|director's commentary]] called ''Imagining BioShock'', featuring the series' creative director [[Ken Levine (game developer)|Ken Levine]] and lead artist Shawn Robertson. Players unlock episodes of the commentary by finding new collectible objects added to the remastered ''BioShock''.<ref>{{cite web |last=McKlusky |first=Kevin |date=August 29, 2016 |url=https://www.destructoid.com/the-new-bioshock-collection-features-developer-commentary-383441.phtml |title=The new BioShock collection features developer commentary |website=[[Destructoid]] |publisher=Enthusiast Gaming |access-date=August 29, 2016 |archive-date=September 24, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160924084539/https://www.destructoid.com/the-new-bioshock-collection-features-developer-commentary-383441.phtml |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Gurwin|first=Gabe|date=August 29, 2016|url=https://www.digitaltrends.com/gaming/bioshock-collection-golden-reels/|title='BioShock: The Collection' gives you even more to collect|website=[[Digital Trends]]|publisher=Designtechnica|access-date=December 10, 2020}}</ref> The remastered games run in [[1080p]] resolution at 60 [[frames per second]] on Xbox One and PlayStation 4.<ref name="IGN: announce">{{cite web |last=Goldfarb |first=Andrew |date=June 30, 2016 |url=http://www.ign.com/articles/2016/06/30/bioshock-the-collection-officially-confirmed-release-date-and-trailer-revealed |title=BioShock: The Collection Officially Confirmed, Release Date and Trailer Revealed |website=[[IGN]]|publisher=Ziff Davis |access-date=June 30, 2016}}</ref>

== Development and release ==
Blind Squirrel Games, who previously worked with ''BioShock'' series developers [[Irrational Games]] on ''BioShock Infinite'',<ref>{{cite web |last=Pagat |first=Mat |date=June 30, 2016 |url=http://www.gamespot.com/articles/bioshock-remastered-collection-confirmed-for-ps4-x/1100-6441390/ |title=BioShock Remastered Collection Confirmed for PS4, Xbox One, and PC |publisher=[[GameSpot]] |access-date=June 30, 2016}}</ref> assisted series producer [[2K (company)|2K]] with development of the remastered collection. 2K decided not to remaster the [[Windows]] edition of ''BioShock Infinite'', which already met their graphical standards for the updated console editions when using its highest graphical settings.<ref name="IGN: announce" /> News of the remastered collection leaked from retailers and trademarks several times in advance of its June 2016 announcement.<ref>{{cite web |last=Schreier |first=Jason |date=June 30, 2016 |url=http://kotaku.com/bioshock-collection-leaks-yet-again-1782831686 |title=BioShock Collection Leaks (Yet Again) [UPDATE: Official] |website=[[Kotaku]] |access-date=June 30, 2016}}</ref><ref name="Polygon: officially announced" />

The collection was released on [[PlayStation 4]] and [[Xbox One]] platforms in North America on September 13, 2016, and worldwide two days later, on September 15, 2016.<ref>{{cite web |last=Frank |first=Allegra |date=September 12, 2016 |url=http://www.polygon.com/2016/9/12/12892556/bioshock-collection-pc-release-date |title=BioShock: The Collection to keep PC players waiting just a little longer |website=[[Polygon (website)|Polygon]]|publisher=Vox Media |access-date=September 12, 2016}}</ref> The collection was released for [[Windows]] on September 15, 2016, and its remastered versions of ''BioShock'' and ''BioShock 2'' were given as upgrades for those who owned the original Windows PC editions.<ref>{{cite web |last=Nunneley |first=Stephany |date=June 30, 2016 |url=https://www.vg247.com/2016/06/30/those-who-own-bioshock-or-bioshock-2-on-steam-get-remaster-upgrade-free/ |title=Those who own BioShock or BioShock 2 on Steam get remaster upgrade free |website=[[VG247]] |publisher=videogaming247 Ltd|access-date=June 30, 2016}}</ref> A [[macOS]] version published by [[Feral Interactive]] released on August 22, 2017.<ref>{{cite web|last=Broussard|
first=Michael|date=August 22, 2017|url=https://www.macrumors.com/2017/08/22/bioshock-remastered-macos/|title='BioShock Remastered' Launches for macOS Computers on Steam, Mac App Store Coming Soon|website=[[MacRumors]]|access-date=December 11, 2020}}</ref> Also produced was a limited run of 450 "Ultra Limited Edition" copies of the game which included an art book, reversible poster, and coin.<ref>{{cite web|last=Goldfarb|first=Andrew|date=September 14, 2016|url=https://www.ign.com/videos/2016/09/14/unboxing-bioshock-the-collections-ultra-limited-edition|title=Unboxing BioShock: The Collection's Ultra Limited Edition|website=[[IGN]]|publisher=Ziff Davis|access-date=December 10, 2020}}</ref> The Xbox One and PlayStation 4 retail release is spread across 2 discs.<ref>{{cite web |last=Sarkar |first=Samit |date=August 17, 2016 | url = http://www.polygon.com/2016/8/17/12490794/bioshock-the-collection-impressions-2-infinite-trailer |title=BioShock: The Collection seems like a worthwhile return to Rapture |website=[[Polygon (website)|Polygon]] |publisher=Vox Media|access-date=August 17, 2016}}</ref>

On release, players of the Windows versions noted that the remastered versions of the games retained bugs and removed graphic options without tweaking configuration files.<ref>{{cite news |last=Meer |first=Alec |date=September 16, 2016 |url=https://www.rockpapershotgun.com/2016/09/16/bioshock-remastered-fixes/ |title=Atlas Sighs: BioShock Remastered PC Is A Bit Of A Mess |website=[[Rock Paper Shotgun]]|publisher=Gamer Network |access-date=September 16, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Paget |first=Mat |date=September 16, 2016 |url=http://www.gamespot.com/articles/bioshock-pc-remasters-having-issues-only-slightly-/1100-6443675/ |title=BioShock PC Remasters Having Issues; Only Slightly Better, Steam Reviews Say |website=[[GameSpot]]|publisher=Red Ventures |access-date=September 16, 2016}}</ref> 2K acknowledged issues with the game,<ref>{{cite web|last=Te|first=Zorine|date=September 20, 2016|url=https://www.gamespot.com/articles/bioshock-pc-remaster-issues-being-addressed-says-2/1100-6443727/|title=BioShock PC Remaster Issues Being Addressed, Says 2K|website=[[GameSpot]]|publisher=Red Ventures|access-date=December 10, 2020}}</ref> and subsequently released a patch in early October 2016 to address a lack of graphics options, crashes, better monitor support and mouse controls.<ref>{{cite web |last=Phillips |first=Tom |date=October 7, 2016 |url=http://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2016-09-20-bioshock-collection-pc-patch-takes-aim-at-mouse-graphical-issues |title=BioShock Collection PC patch takes aim at mouse, graphical issues |website=[[Eurogamer]]|publisher=Gamer Network|access-date=October 7, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Paget |first=Mat |date=October 7, 2016 |url=http://www.gamespot.com/articles/new-bioshock-pc-remasters-patch-fixes-multiple-iss/1100-6444277/ |title=New BioShock PC Remasters Patch Fixes Multiple Issues |website=[[GameSpot]]| publisher=Red Ventures |access-date=October 7, 2016}}</ref>

In 2020, enhancement patches were released to increase the resolution of the games when played on Xbox One X and PlayStation 4 Pro. The patch boosted the resolution of the first two games to [[1440p]] on PS4 Pro and [[2160p]] on Xbox One X, and 1440p for both consoles for ''Infinite''.<ref>{{cite web|last=Battaglia|first=Alex|date=June 4, 2020|url=https://www.eurogamer.net/articles/digitalfoundry-2020-bioshock-the-collection-ps4-pro-xbox-one-x-patch-test|title=BioShock: The Collection gets upgraded for PS4 Pro and Xbox One X - and the results disappoint|website=[[Eurogamer]]|publisher=Gamer Network|access-date=December 10, 2020}}</ref>  The collection was also released on the Nintendo Switch in May. It maintains the upgraded assets for the remasters of ''BioShock'' and ''BioShock 2'', and runs at 1080p at 30 frames per second when docked, dropping to [[720p]] in portable mode.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Morgan |first1=Thomas |title=BioShock: The Collection for Switch - classic games get a solid remaster |url=https://www.eurogamer.net/articles/digitalfoundry-2020-bioshock-the-collection-switch-port-analysis |website=[[Eurogamer]]|date=June 6, 2020 |publisher=Gamer Network |access-date=June 7, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.polygon.com/nintendo/2020/3/26/21195331/nintendo-switch-direct-mini-release-date-announcements-bioshock-borderlands|title=BioShock, Borderlands games coming to Nintendo Switch in May|date=March 26, 2020|website=[[Polygon (website)|Polygon]]|publisher=Vox Media|first=Nicole|last=Carpenter|access-date=March 26, 2020}}</ref>

''BioShock: The Collection'' received "generally favorable" reviews according to video game [[review aggregator]] website [[Metacritic]], with platform scores between 80 and 84 out of 100.<ref name="MCPS4" /><ref name="MCXONE" /><ref name="MCPC" /><ref name="MCNS" /> Critics generally recommended the collection for players unfamiliar with the franchise, as well as returning players,<ref name="gamerev-bioshock collection review"/><ref name="digitalspy-bioshock collection review">{{cite web|last=Andrews|first=Stuart|date=September 16, 2016|url=https://www.digitalspy.com/videogames/a808125/bioshock-the-collection-review/|title=BioShock: The Collection review – The best way to play|website=[[Digital Spy]]|publisher=Hearst Magazines UK|access-date=December 10, 2020}}</ref> though others, such as ''IGN''{{'}}s Jonathon Dornbush, felt that the collection's appeal to longtime players was less clear.<ref name="ign-bioshock collection review"/><ref name="inside gamer-bioshock collection review"/>

''[[Game Revolution]]''{{'}}s Peter Paras praised the updated visuals for the first two games, although they also noted that they felt dated graphically compared to modern games.<ref name="gamerev-bioshock collection review"/> While reviews generally noted improved performance on most games,<ref name="ign-bioshock collection review"/> others highlighted frame rate inconsistencies that ''Infinite'' still suffered from.<ref name="digitalspy-bioshock collection review"/><ref name="inside gamer-bioshock collection review"/><ref name="windowscentral-bioshock collection review">{{cite web|last=Brown|first=Matt|date=September 30, 2016|url=https://www.windowscentral.com/bioshock-collection-review|title=BioShock Collection Review|website=Windows Central|publisher=Future plc|access-date=December 15, 2020}}</ref> The games' atmosphere was regarded to have remained intact and effective, beyond the aging of the graphics themselves.<ref name="telegraph-bioshock collection review">{{cite news|last=White|first=Sam|date=September 21, 2016|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/gaming/what-to-play/bioshock-the-collection-review---a-wonder-to-revisit-rapture/|title=BioShock: The Collection Review—A Wonder to Revisit Rapture|newspaper=[[The Daily Telegraph]]|access-date=December 15, 2020}}</ref><ref name="inside gamer-bioshock collection review"/>

''[[Nintendo Life]]'' noted that the earlier game's lack of more recent genre conventions such as [[Glossary of video game terms#ADS|aim down sights]] or sprinting gave them a decidedly "old school" feel that took time to get acclimated to.<ref name="nintendolife-bioshock collection review">{{cite web|last=Vogel|first=Mitch|date=June 8, 2020|url=https://www.nintendolife.com/reviews/nintendo-switch/bioshock_the_collection|title=BioShock: The Collection Review (Switch)|website=Nintendo Life|publisher=Gamer Network|access-date=December 10, 2020}}</ref> More critically, ''Insider Gamer''{{'}}s Derek Taal said that the gameplay of the early games had aged poorly, and occasionally proved frustrating.<ref name="inside gamer-bioshock collection review">{{cite web|last=Taal|first=Derek|date=September 24, 2016|url=https://www.insidegamer.nl/recensies/124891/bioshock-collection-review-atlas-haalt-zijn-schouders-op|title=BioShock Collection Review: Atlas Shrugs|website=InsideGamer.nl|publisher=Reshift Digital|language=nl|access-date=December 15, 2020|archive-date=July 29, others lamented that most of the improvements were for the first ''BioShock'' and the subsequent titles received less attention.<ref name="ign-bioshock collection review"/><ref name="gamerev-bioshock collection review"/><ref name="digitalspy-bioshock collection review"/><ref name="windowscentral-bioshock collection review"/> Other criticisms included inconsistent controls between games<ref
